title: An Oracle-Free Quantum Algorithm for Nonadiabatic Quantum Molecular Dynamics
summary: Quantum computation is an attractive front for many problems that are intractable for computers today. One such problem is nonadiabatic quantum molecular dynamics, where quantized internal states coupling to parameterized modes result in a Hamiltonian resistant to oracle-based models and spectral decomposition. This dissertation applies diabatic Hamiltonian operators directly to the computational basis as first-quantized split-operator propagators, validated with dynamic observables including absorption and recurrence spectra, scattering cross-sections, population dynamics, and quantum…
